task: Project the approved REVIEW Finding triage policy into all active REVIEW Agent prompts without amending Dynamic Finding authority or runtime mechanics.
outcome: The generated prompt for each of the five canonical REVIEW Agents displays the same English Finding triage contract, including “severity and applicability are separate axes,” evidence-backed routing, fail-closed unknown applicability, and bounded current-Story repair; non-REVIEW prompts do not display that contract.
facts: The Dynamic Finding System execution plan is authoritative and remains unchanged by this Story.
The proposal is a subordinate Agent-side projection, not a runtime or authority amendment.
Five canonical active REVIEW lanes consume centrally assembled prompts in full-envelope and legacy-full-context modes.
Retired verdict vocabulary may appear only in historical evidence or negative test inputs, never as an active Task Context alias.
Role-contract requiredCheckIds are declarative metadata and are not execution or gate evidence.
Current finding_dismiss compatibility behavior changes current blocking status but proves neither applicability, repair, resolution, nor deferral.
CHK-005 and CHK-006 are separately reviewed acceptance/identity infrastructure repairs needed for truthful Story evidence.
constraints: All new proposal and Agent-facing prose must be English.
Severity, evidenceState, applicability, disposition, and gate impact remain separate axes.
Unknown applicability fails closed when the Finding would otherwise block.
Reviewers do not repair, dismiss, create follow-up Stories, use gap_log for product routing, rewrite severity, or widen scope.
Do not modify Dynamic Finding schemas, handlers, predicates, process-fact registries, lifecycle gates, or its authority document.
Use RED then GREEN and verify the final committed source through the local CLI.
